newsitem.title: MACAU: Man shot in restaurant in Macau casino turf war.
newsitem.headline: Man shot in restaurant in Macau casino turf war.

text.p: A man was shot and seriously wounded in a Macau restaurant on Wednesday night in what appeared to be another casualty in a triad gang war over casino rackets, police said.
Ng Yue-chuen, 44, was dining with friends at the busy Mou Kei restaurant when he was shot by a lone gunman, witnesses said.
"That man came in, fired one shot at him from close range and then just walked away," a witness told Reuters.
The gunman fled on a motor scooter, an assassin's favourite getaway vehicle here, through the Portuguese-ruled enclave's narrow alleyways, he said.
Police sources said the shooting appeared to be yet another act of violence in months of casino-related gangster rivalry marked by arson attacks, bombings and drive-by shootings.

At least 17 people have been killed this year in the turf wars, in which secret criminal societies known as triads are vying for the proceeds of illegal loansharking and protection rackets that feed off Macau's legal casinos, the enclave's biggest industry.
Ng underwent surgery in hospital to remove a bullet from his lower abdomen, doctors said, adding he was likely to survive.
Casino monopoly holder Stanley Ho said last week he believed the clashes between triad gangs on the fringes of his nine casinos in Macau were "almost over".
Macau, a tiny territory of 450,000 people on the Pearl River Delta, returns to Chinese sovereignty in 1999 after four and a half centuries of Portuguese rule.
